newsitem.title: CHINA: China army brass warns future HK unit of problems.
newsitem.headline: China army brass warns future HK unit of problems.

text.p: The Chinese military unit to be stationed in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Beijing rule in 1997 could face unexpected problems, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday, quoting one of China's top generals.

Liu Huaqing, vice-chairman of the powerful Central Military Commission, urged the People's Liberation Army (PLA) unit to be stationed in Hong Kong next year to present a good image to the territory's residents, Xinhua said.
"Liu expressed satisfaction with the unit's preparatory work, but cautioned that they might meet unexpected problems," Xinhua said without elaborating.
Liu had made his remarks during an inspection on Monday of the PLA unit, now posted in the booming southern city of Shenzhen, the agency said.
"He urged the officers and soldiers to lay a solid foundation politically and militarily to enhance their ability to cope with various situations," it said.
Liu had urged the unit to pay attention to discipline and to "deal properly with Hong Kong residents", Xinhua said.
Hong Kong, which will revert to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997, after 150 years of British rule, views the arrival of Chinese troops with some wariness.
Images of the bloody June 1989 military crackdown on student-led protests for more democracy in Beijing's Tiananmen Square remain vivid in the minds of many Hong Kong residents.
